lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: Listen. Then act it out develops listening comprehension and builds understanding of simple actions. Students listen for key instructions and show their comprehension by acting them out with clear movements.
Look for careful listening, correction actions and students joining in with the activity.
“I have a friend coming for dinner tonight, I’m not sure what to cook. Let’s read this story and see if it gives me any ideas!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - B Look and choose

details: Look and choose allows students to recognise key food vocabulary by linking it to simple yes/no questions. The activity reinforces meaning as students look at the pictures and choose the correct answer.
Look for students checking each picture carefully, choosing correct answers, and using the question form from the model to guide their decisions.
“I think I’ve got oranges and apples, so I could  make a fruit tart! Help me check that I’ve got the ingredients!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - A Read and number

details: Read and number develops reading and comprehension through ordering a story, reinforcing comprehension and reading fluency and pronunciation with accurate word stress.
Look for correct and logical story order, clear pronunciation, accurate word and phrase stress, confident reading.
“Hmm, should I make something sweet using fruit? What sort of fruit do you like to eat?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Set:
Complete an example of the homework to check Ss understanding. Have Ss then write the homework page, activity and plan in their diaries. 
Leaderboard:
Show the Leaderboard and congratulate / encourage daily app practise.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - C Make your own story

details: Make your own story develops creative writing skills by asking students to create a short story. It supports imagination, sentence building and meaningful language use.
Look for stories that show clear ideas and accurate spelling, as well as use of key vocabulary about fruit and vegetables from the lesson.
“What would you make if you had a friend coming for dinner? Make your own story!”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - Tongue Twisters Listen and say

details: Tongue Twisters: Listen and say helps students practice pronunciation and repetition of tricky sounds as they listen and repeat the tongue twisters.
Look for careful listening, confident pronunciation and accurate repetition of tricky sounds.
All your meals sound delicious! Will you bring in any leftovers for our next class?
